paper: arXiv:1606.06011 (Aboulker, Matamala, Rochet, Zamora, 2016) -- A new class of graphs that satisfies the Chen-Chvatal conjecture
title: Counter-examples to the lines+bridges inequality ell(G)+br(G) >= |G|
_round_note: Phase 0 substrate. Exact BFS-distance oracle built and verified against the paper's known small-graph data (C4: ell=1, br=0; full connected-graph census n=4..7 reproduced exactly: 1/4/4/2 counter-examples with bridgeless splits 1/4/3/0). Engine-ready.
central_question: The Chen-Chvatal 'lines' inequality asks: does every connected graph G satisfy ell(G)+br(G) >= |G|, where ell(G) is the number of distinct metric lines and br(G) is the number of bridges? It is FALSE in general (C4 is the smallest counter-example: ell=1, br=0, n=4). The paper's open Conjecture 2.2 ('finite generating family') asserts that every counter-example arises from a FINITE list of graphs by replacing a bridge with a path -- i.e. the bridge-containing minimal counter-examples are finite up to that path-substitution closure. That asymptotic claim is not directly decidable by enumeration, but the underlying testable predicate ell+br>=n and the discovery/classification of all small counter-examples (especially the bridge-containing minimal ones the conjecture is about, beyond the three known Figure-2 graphs) is fully oracle-able by exact small-instance computation.

benchmark.description: The fixed yardstick. The predicate ell(G)+br(G) >= |G| on connected graphs, and the exact counter-example census by order n. All quantities are EXACT integer combinatorics from BFS distances + nx.bridges (no heuristics, no SAT).
benchmark.predicate: ell(G) + br(G) >= |G| = n  (counter-example iff ell+br < n)
benchmark.ell: number of DISTINCT metric lines; line(a,b) = {a,b} U {x : [abx] or [axb] or [xab]}, [pqr] := d(p,q)+d(q,r)=d(p,r}

ground_truth_landmarks.C4: ell(C4)=1 (single universal line on all 4 vertices), br(C4)=0, n=4 => ell+br=1<4; the UNIQUE smallest counter-example and it is BRIDGELESS. Oracle reproduced ell(C4)=1 exactly.
ground_truth_landmarks.census_n4: 6 connected graphs; 1 counter-example (1 bridgeless, 0 with bridge) = C4
ground_truth_landmarks.census_n5: 21 connected graphs; 4 counter-examples (4 bridgeless, 0 with bridge)
ground_truth_landmarks.census_n6: 112 connected graphs; 4 counter-examples (3 bridgeless, 1 with bridge)
ground_truth_landmarks.census_n7: 853 connected graphs; 2 counter-examples (0 bridgeless, 2 with bridge)
ground_truth_landmarks.bridge_counterexamples_n7: two witnesses, both with bridges: (i) ell=4 br=2 lhs=6<7, bridges {0-3,0-4}; (ii) ell=4 br=1 lhs=5<7, bridge {2-4}
ground_truth_landmarks.verified_by_oracle: All of the above RAN via scripts/oracle.py enumerate {4,5,6,7} and matched the paper's stated counts exactly; 6/6 regression tests pass in ~0.2s

proved.claim: ell(G)+br(G) >= |G| is FALSE in general; C4 is a counter-example (ell=1, br=0, n=4)
proved.source: paper; INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by oracle (ell(C4)=1 single universal line, br=0)

proved.claim: Exact counter-example census for connected graphs: n=4:1, n=5:4, n=6:4, n=7:2 counter-examples; bridgeless splits 1/4/3/0 respectively
proved.source: oracle full geng -c enumeration; matches the paper's stated small-graph data

proved.claim: All n<=5 counter-examples are BRIDGELESS; bridge-containing counter-examples first appear at n=6 (one) and n=7 (two)
proved.source: oracle census; relevant because Conjecture 2.2 is about the bridge-containing family

open_crux: Conjecture 2.2 (paper): every counter-example to ell+br>=|G| is obtained from a FINITE set of graphs by replacing a bridge with a path. This is an asymptotic/structural claim NOT directly settled by finite enumeration. The oracle-able stress test: enumerate every small counter-example, classify bridgeless vs bridge-containing, and check whether any NEW minimal bridge-containing counter-example appears that is NOT reducible to the three known Figure-2 graphs by bridge->path replacement. A new irreducible minimal bridge counter-example at some order n would REFUTE the finiteness; persistent reducibility is empirical support only (empirical != proof). Secondary measurable: do bridgeless counter-examples remain finite/structured, or do new families appear with n?

live_hypotheses.idea: Conjecture 2.2 holds: the bridge-containing minimal counter-examples form a finite list closed under bridge->path replacement. Test by enumerating bridge counter-examples for n=6,7,8,... and checking each reduces (collapse each bridge to a single edge / shortest representative) to one of the three known Figure-2 graphs.
live_hypotheses.predicts: Every bridge-containing minimal counter-example at every reachable n reduces by bridge-contraction to a fixed finite set (the three Figure-2 graphs); no new irreducible minimal bridge counter-example appears.
live_hypotheses.note: Phase 0: oracle confirms bridge counter-examples start at n=6 (one) and n=7 (two). NEXT: implement bridge->path contraction normalization in the oracle and a 'reduces-to-known-3' check; extend census to n=8,9 (geng -c grows fast: ~11k at n=8, ~261k at n=9 connected graphs -- feasible; ell is O(n^3), bridges O(n+m)). A single irreducible new minimal bridge CE kills the conjecture.

live_hypotheses.idea: Characterize the bridgeless counter-examples. They dominate small n (1/4/3/0 at n=4..7). Determine whether they form a structured/finite family or grow -- the paper treats bridgeless counter-examples separately from the bridge family of Conj 2.2.
live_hypotheses.predicts: Bridgeless counter-examples are either finite or fall into an identifiable structured family (e.g. small-diameter / few-distinct-lines graphs like C4, C5); their count does NOT blow up combinatorially with n.
live_hypotheses.source: oracle census observation (bridgeless count 1->4->3->0 over n=4..7)
live_hypotheses.note: The vanishing of bridgeless CEs at n=7 is suggestive but small-n; needs n=8,9 to see if the bridgeless family truly thins out or revives. Few-distinct-lines is the structural driver (ell small forces ell+br<n).

decision_log.note: Phase 0 substrate built. Folder scaffolded (scripts/data/tests/docs/Refs); shared venv symlinked. EXACT oracle implemented WITHOUT SAT (this is an undirected-graph metric problem, not a digraph one): scripts/core.py = BFS all-pairs distances + metric-betweenness line construction (line(a,b)={a,b} U {x : one of [abx],[axb],[xab]}) + distinct-line count ell + nx.bridges count br + geng -c connected-graph enumerator; scripts/oracle.py = check_construction / enumerate_counterexamples / CLI (check, enumerate, edges). VERIFIED against the paper's known data: C4 gives ell=1 (single universal line {0,1,2,3}), br=0, ell+br=1<4 -- reproduced exactly; full connected-graph census n=4..7 reproduced exactly (counts 1/4/4/2; bridgeless splits 1/4/3/0; n=6 has 1 bridge CE, n=7 has 2 bridge CEs). 6/6 regression tests pass in 0.2s. Ledger seeded (P1-P3 from oracle+paper, open_crux = Conjecture 2.2 finiteness, H1 bridge-family finiteness, H2 bridgeless characterization). Census JSONs cached in data/.

next_action: Drive H1: implement bridge->path contraction normalization + a 'reduces-to-the-three-known-Figure-2-graphs' check in the oracle, then extend the EXACT census to n=8 (and n=9 if tractable) and report whether any NEW irreducible minimal bridge-containing counter-example appears (which would REFUTE Conjecture 2.2) or whether all reduce to the known three (empirical support only). In parallel measure H2 (bridgeless CE count + their distinct-line structure) at n=8,9.

discipline_gates.empirical_not_proof: A finite-n census confirming Conjecture 2.2 (all bridge CEs reduce to the known three) is VERIFICATION, not a proof of the asymptotic finiteness claim -- it stays in live_hypotheses. Only a refutation (a new irreducible minimal bridge counter-example) is a hard finite-certificate result that can be promoted to proved[]. The predicate ell+br<n and individual graph measurements ARE exact certificates and may be promoted.
discipline_gates.audit_not_redteam: Grounding (oracle measurement of ell, br on a proposed graph) and skeptic (search for a counter-example to a structural sub-claim, e.g. an irreducible new bridge CE) are separate steps, never the same agent call.
discipline_gates.citations_verified: Any external citation (Chen-Chvatal conjecture, the three Figure-2 graphs, Conjecture 2.2 statement) must resolve to the primary source arXiv:1606.06011 before it carries weight; the Figure-2 graphs must be transcribed from the PDF, not assumed.
